items.title: Just announced: The Mississauga Mayoral Debate
items.summary: The debate will take place at the Mississauga Civic Centre, in the heart of the city’s downtown. We cover provincial politics, with an obsession for three things: politics, policies and personalities. Every now and then, all three break free of the Pink Palace. This time, the action is in Mississauga, where much of the political drama in the race for mayor — featuring two of only three people to hold the job since 1978 — is provincial through and through. Expected to be one of the province’s “most watched” mayoral contests, it even had Etobicoke-born Premier Doug Ford weighing in months before it began. “You know something, I never get involved in municipal elections, but I will send an army down here to make sure I support Mayor (Carolyn) Parrish,” Ford said at a Mississauga construction site in March. ” In other words: this is our kind of mayoral race. An incumbent supported by Mr. Ford and his caucus, challenged by her predecessor, the three-term mayor who quit to become Liberal leader and spent much of the past three years on the other side of the Ford government. Two returning challengers who placed second and third the last time around, competing for many of the same organizers and networks Crombie had long relied on. For a publication built to cover provincial politics, there’s simply too much of it in this race to ignore. So, on Monday, Oct. 5, we’re hosting a debate. “The Mississauga Mayoral Debate” will bring together the leading mayoral candidates for a 90-minute debate on the future of the province’s fourth-largest city.

items.title: Mississauga man linked to deaths worldwide faces sentencing
items.summary: Friends and relatives of those who took their own lives using items bought online from Kenneth Law are expected to lay bare their loss in court in the coming days as the Ontario man linked to dozens of deaths worldwide faces a sentencing hearing. , pleaded guilty in late May to 14 counts of aiding suicide in the deaths of 14 people in the province, including some who were minors. The plea deal came weeks after Law was set to stand trial on the charges and another 14 counts of first-degree murder related to the same victims. Prosecutors have said they plan to withdraw the murder charges after Law is sentenced. Those found guilty of aiding suicide can face up to 14 years in prison, and lawyers for the Crown and the defence are expected to present what they believe would be an appropriate sentence as part of the hearing set to begin today. The hearing also offers loved ones of those who died an opportunity to tell Law and the court how his actions affected them. Law ran several websites that were used to sell sodium nitrite and other products that can be used for self-harm, according to an agreed statement of fact read in court after his plea. He sent some 1,200 packages to people in more than 40 countries, including close to 160 packages shipped to addresses within Canada, the document said.

items.title: 23 guns seized, 4 arrested in Peel police operation
items.summary: These guns have been linked to 14 shootings across the GTA and one fatal shooting in Missisauga, say police. Peel police have announced an update on Project Red Zone. Peel Regional Police have seized 23 guns and 950 rounds of ammunition associated with a firearms trafficking network. One of the guns has been linked to a fatal shooting in Mississauga, and 14 have been linked to shootings across the GTA, said Peel police. The announcement, shared on Tuesday, came as an update to a nine-month undercover investigation called Project Red Zone. Four people have been arrested and charged as a result of the investigation. Two have been released and two were held pending a bail hearing. Megan Mills Devoe is a staff reporter with the Toronto Star.

items.title: Early 2027 Launch Planned as Mississauga Opens Its Whistleblower Hotline to the Public
items.summary: According to a staff report set to go before Mississauga's general committee on Wednesday, the city plans to launch an expanded whistleblower hotline for residents sometime in the first three months of 2027. The city established its original Whistleblower Program in 2014, giving employees a confidential channel to anonymously flag workplace wrongdoing, but the new fraud and waste hotline will extend that same option to the general public. Amy Truong, the city's internal audit director, wrote in the report that the program has spent the past decade supporting accountability, ethical conduct and a workplace culture where concerns can be raised without fear of reprisal. The report describes the expanded hotline as an independent and confidential reporting mechanism meant to strengthen accountability and reinforce public trust in the integrity of city operations. Once it is running, both city workers and members of the public will be able to use it to report concerns tied to fraud, waste or wrongdoing that could affect the city's operations. Truong's report also frames the changes as an effort to strengthen transparency and public confidence in how the city governs and oversees itself. The move follows discussions among councillors and staff back in March about whether Mississauga should also hire an auditor general to bolster public accountability.

items.title: Gun call leads to 4 arrests and $65K in seized drugs in Mississauga
items.summary: A report of a man sitting in a car with a gun in the heart of Mississauga has led police to four arrests and the recovery of an estimated $65,000 in drugs. Peel Regional Police said the initial call was received just over two weeks ago, on Sept. 7, when it was reported that a man in a vehicle was armed with a gun in the area of Hurontario and Dundas streets in the Cooksville neighbourhood. Once on the scene, police officers quickly located a man who was found to be in possession of an illegal firearm and a separate magazine containing ammunition, police said. The responding officers also located and seized “a quantity of suspected cocaine and fentanyl with an estimated value of $65,000,” Peel police said on Tuesday. A man was subsequently arrested by officers with the Peel police 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau. Following further investigation and the execution of a search warrant at a Mississauga residence, three additional people were arrested, according to police.

items.title: A Report of an Armed Man in Cooksville Led Police to Four Arrests and $65,000 in Drugs
items.summary: According to CTV News, Peel Regional Police say four people have been arrested after a September 7 call reporting a man armed with a gun inside a vehicle near Hurontario Street and Dundas Street West, in the city's Cooksville area. Officers who responded found the man in possession of an illegal firearm along with a separate loaded magazine, according to police. A search of the scene turned up a quantity of suspected cocaine and fentanyl that police estimated to be worth about $65,000. Investigators later executed a search warrant at a Mississauga residence, where three more people were arrested. Police say Olamilekan Jimoh, 26, of Mississauga, faces the most charges, including careless storage of a firearm, failing to comply with an undertaking, and four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking. Modupe Abijo, 52, and Omobodunrin Jimoh, 28, both of Mississauga, were each charged with four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking, while Cleo Romi Reynods, 45, of Toronto, was charged with failing to comply with a release order.

items.title: Mississauga’s staff-only whistleblower program is being reshaped into a public hotline residents may use by 2027
items.summary: After the unanimous vote, councillors stood for a moment of … Drivers — not homeowners — would face the fine under the pro… Residents will be able to anonymously report financial misuse and wrongdoing at city hall — a program previously open only to staff since 2014. A staff report outlines the plan for the city’s Fraud and Waste Hotline, expected to launch in early 2027 for the public. By early 2027, Mississauga residents could begin reporting municipal fraud and financial waste through the city’s Fraud and Waste Hotline. A report is coming to general committee on Sept. 23 which outlines an implementation plan on how the city’s existing internal whistleblower program will be made public and renamed as the Fraud and Waste Hotline. The move follows a staff report in March, which came in response to resident demands for better financial oversight. In the report, staff provided four recommendations and council opted to expand the internal audit division.
